title: Singapore's Response to Current Global COVID-19 Situation
what_it_is: Singapore's Response to Current Global COVID-19 Situation

sections.label: Imported infections share of cases
sections.summary: Imported infections account for about 5% to 10% of total cases reported daily.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Imported infections today account for about 5% to 10% of the total cases reported every day.

sections.label: Travellers from China testing positive
sections.summary: In the four weeks to 1 January 2023, about 200 travellers from China tested COVID-19 positive, under 5% of imported infections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: During that time, that four weeks, there were about 200 travellers from China detected to be COVID-19 positive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, for the whole four weeks running up to 1 January 2023, 200 travellers from China were detected to be COVID-19 positive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They accounted for less than 5% of our total imported infections.

sections.label: Weekly flights from China
sections.summary: Singapore currently runs 38 weekly flights from China, compared to around 400 pre-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of now, we run 38 weekly flights from China to Singapore, compared to around 400 flights pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Countries' PDT requirements for China travellers
sections.summary: Several countries impose a 100% PDT requirement on travellers from China, while Singapore and Spain require vaccination or a negative PDT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, several countries, namely, Australia, Canada, and several EU countries, such as Belgium, France, Germany, Sweden, India, Japan, UK and the US, they are imposing a 100% PDT requirement on all travellers from China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And then, the third category, just Singapore and Spain, which have the policy of either you are fully vaccinated or produce a negative PDT result.

sections.label: ICU cases and deaths in 30 days
sections.summary: In the past 30 days, ICU COVID-19 patients were in the low single digit and 25 days had no deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To illustrate, in the past 30 days, the number of COVID-19 patients in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) is in the low single digit, and there were 25 days out of the 30 days where there were no COVID-19 deaths.

sections.label: Peak of year-end XBB wave
sections.summary: At last year's year-end XBB variant peak, the seven-day moving average infection was over 8,500 cases a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To illustrate again, at the peak of the year-end XBB variant wave last year, we were registering a seven-day moving average infection of over 8,500 cases a day.

sections.label: Chinese regions sharing viral genomes
sections.summary: Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Fujian and Inner Mongolia contribute weekly viral genome sequences to GISAID.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Fujian and Inner Mongolia contribute up-to-date viral genome sequences to GISAID on a weekly basis.

sections.label: GISAID data gaps and variants
sections.summary: GISAID is working with Chinese authorities to expand data capture; data shows China's epidemic is driven by BA.5.2 and BF.7.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There are still gaps in the data, so GISAID is working with the Chinese authorities to expand the data capture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So far, the data shows that the epidemic in China is driven by variants that are well-known and have been circulating in other regions of the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The dominating ones are BA.5.2, as well as BF.7.

sections.label: Increasing Singapore-China flights
sections.summary: Minister Iswaran will explain increasing Singapore-China flights as China's wave subsides, without compromising Singaporeans' health and healthcare resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Minister Iswaran will explain how we will increase the number of flights between Singapore and China in a calibrated fashion, as the infection wave continues to subside in China, while ensuring that the health of Singaporeans and healthcare resources are not compromised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I reported earlier that over the past four weeks, travellers from China accounted for less than 5% of imported infections, and one out of seven severe cases.

sections.label: Travellers from China infection share
sections.summary: About 200 travellers from China tested COVID-19 positive, under 5% of imported infections and under 1% of total infections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: During that time, there were about 200 travellers from China detected to be COVID-19 positive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They accounted for less than 5% of our total imported infections, and less than 1% of our total infections.

sections.label: Imported severe cases by region
sections.summary: Last December, seven imported cases developed severe illness and were hospitalised: three from the Middle East, two from ASEAN, one each from China and Europe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Last December, amongst all the imported cases, seven developed severe illnesses and had to be hospitalised – three were from the Middle East, two from ASEAN, and one each from China and Europe.

sections.label: Weekly flights from China
sections.summary: Singapore currently runs 38 weekly flights from China, compared to around 400 flights pre-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of now, we run 38 weekly flights from China, compared to around 400 flights pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Vaccination uptake and bivalent vaccines
sections.summary: About 60% of individuals aged 16 and above are up to date with vaccinations, and about 13,000 take the bivalent vaccine daily.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of 31 December 2022, about 60% of individuals aged 16 and above are up to date with their vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, about 13,000 individuals are taking the bivalent vaccine on a daily basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And now, with the introduction of the bivalent formulations for both Moderna and Pfizer – we have two brands to choose from – I hope more will step forward to get better protection.

sections.label: Possible final adjustment of restrictions
sections.summary: If the situation stays stable after year-end travel and China's infection wave, remaining social restrictions can be finally adjusted for post-pandemic normalcy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister said in his New Year's Day message, if the situation continues to be stable after the year-end travel season and the infection wave in China, we can look forward to making final adjustments to our remaining social restrictions to establish a post-pandemic normalcy.
